**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Sparkling:

- **§ 3 (Restrictions on Use)** — the only covenant section binding us — is confined to standard licence-scope protections (backup-only copying, no sublicence/export, no reverse engineering, "not use the Work except as authorized herein"). Nothing limits the products we may buy, build, or market.
- **§ 2 (Grant of License)** is a non-exclusive licence with no exclusivity, minimum-volume, or sole-source commitment.
- **§ 19** is a mutual employee non-solicitation (one year, both parties) — a personnel covenant, not a business restriction; it belongs to the non-solicitation rule and I have not double-flagged it here.
- Targeted searches for "compet", "similar", "exclusiv", and "shall not develop" surfaced only unrelated usages (competence of project managers, non-exclusive jurisdiction, force majeure).

This satisfies the **preferred** position, so no narrowing fallback is needed.
